title: Special Edition: The Shield Hero’s Valentine’s Day Part 5
text: “Come to think of it, Atla isn’t here.”
“Atla-chan is with Fohl-kun. Didn’t Naofumi-sama tell you to keep her under control today because she’d be in the way?”

Come to think of it, that’s right. Thanks to the gloves that allow him to grasp Atla—who is a spirit—Fohl has been able to touch her. Thanks to the accessory that provides warmth, he can now endure the cold to some extent and move around a bit more freely. And since he’s keeping that noisy little imp, Atla, under control, it’s a total win-win. Just like my little brother.
“Ah, Naofumi-sama. How are you today?”
Atla, held by Fohl, came over. She’s reaching out her hand toward me for some reason. Does she really hate being with her big brother that much?
“Big bro, what were you up to today?”
“Hm? I ran some errands before noon. After that, I was working on a prototype for my next business venture.”
“What’s this black stuff? Is it edible?”
Apparently, Fohl doesn’t know. Well, I can’t imagine chocolate ever having played a role in Fohl’s life.
“This is chocolate. It’s a sweet, but… since it grows on a plant, does that make it a fruit…?”

For now, I put my doubts aside and gave Fohl a detailed explanation about chocolate. I framed it as a seasonal rite of passage where you give it to someone you like. Incidentally, for some reason, Atla already knew about it. I wonder what kind of difference there is in these two’s information networks.
“Naofumi-sama, I’m really going to go all out for Valentine’s Day.”
“Ah, yeah, yeah. As for Fohl—…”
He’s actually pretty popular in the village, but Fohl doesn’t seem to be interested in anyone other than Atla. Looks like this is going to be a pointless event.
“I hope I get some chocolate from Atla.”
And so, I muttered this impossible dream.
“Ah, uh…”
Huh? Fohl’s reaction seems a bit slow. He was over the moon when he got his Christmas present, though.

After that, we all had a snack together, and the village cooking team was teaching those who wanted to make chocolate how to do it. For some reason, even monsters and Filolials seemed to be going over to learn. As soon as Melty realized she could procure chocolate for sale in the village, she accepted it and headed out with Filo. Days passed like this.
“Come on, Gaelion. Good morning, good morning, okay? Come on.”
“Cureee… Cureee”
Amidst these daily routines, I noticed Taniko doing something face-to-face with Gaelion. I happened to be out alone, taking a walk to clear my head while preparing for my next peddling trip.
“What are you doing?”
“Hm? I’m thinking of teaching Gaelion to speak soon.”
“Oh, really?”
“Gaelion’s a special dragon, right?”
“Yeah, apparently he’s the Dragon Emperor.”

Most of the Dragon Emperor’s fragments currently reside within Gaelion. Gaelion is already practically the king of dragons. He did reasonably well in the battle against that damn goddess, and his parent Gaelion is the one who’ll perform the limit break. Well, from my perspective, he’s just a lackluster, disappointing Dragon Emperor.
“Cure…”
The young Gaelion glanced at me with a somewhat troubled look.
“It’s because you dislike monsters that understand human speech,”
The adult Gaelion muttered telepathically. Huh? So the young Gaelion isn’t talking because I’m a talking monster—and that’s not his type?
“Rafu?”
“Oh? Isn’t that Raph-chan?”
Raph-chan, who had been on a salvage expedition with Sadeena, happened to show up just then and ran right up to climb onto me.
“Cure!”
Gaelion leaped onto me too, as if trying to one-up her.
“Whoa, hey!”
“Raph-chan?”
“Cure?”
Then, both of them tilted their heads in unison. Oh, so they’re not going to fight after all. I guess the Raph-species is treated differently from that chatty bird over there.
“Hey, Gaelion. Come over here and learn some manners!”
Taniko scolded Gaelion as if she were his mother. But Gaelion clung to me, refusing to let go, as if he hadn’t a care in the world.
“Seriously! You’ll never become a proper dragon if you act like that!”
You’re already the world’s greatest dragon, aren’t you? I’ll keep that to myself, though. After all, Gaelion is still in his young dragon form right now.
“Speaking of which, does Raph-chan take part in things like Valentine’s Day?”
The monsters seemed really interested in chocolate too—I wonder if Raph-chan participates in events like this?
“Raph-chan?”
“Cure?”

It’s cute when these two tilt their heads like that. These two monsters who choose not to speak… well, one of them does talk nonstop when she switches to telepathy—or rather, when her other personality takes over. They’re both still just as clingy as ever. I pet both of their heads and set them down.
“Aren’t chocolates poisonous to monsters?”
Taniko and Rat would know the answer to that. Though Rat has been going out on fieldwork with Taniko more often lately, so he’s hardly ever in the village anymore.
“That old lady said it depends on the species. Dragons are fine with chocolate.”
“Hmm… As for the Raph-species… I guess there’s no way to know.”

I think it’s probably fine. If you gave it to a real tanuki or a dog, it’d be toxic and dangerous, but Raph-chan should be okay. Similarly, Keel doesn’t seem to have any problems with chocolate either, so I’m just winging it on this one.
“Does the Shield Hero like chocolate?”
When Taniko asks me that, I fall deep in thought. Hmm… If you ask me whether I like it or not, it’s kind of hard to say.
“To be honest, there are times when I really don’t get what’s so great about that stuff. I’ve handed it out before, but… apparently, in my world, chocolate was originally classified as a medicine.”
Ah, that’s why the quality is surprisingly good even though I just make it on a whim. I guess the alchemy bonus and the cooking bonus are both kicking in.
“Oil… Hehehehehehe.”
Taniko lets out a creepy, cackling laugh. Like… that kind of smirk where one corner of her mouth is turned up and her eyes are shaped like crescent moons?
She has such a creepy laugh. I feel like she’s gradually becoming less human. She used to be more pure, right? She’s slowly starting to go off the rails in a bad way.
We’re going to be in big trouble if we don’t get her straightened out somewhere… What’s causing this?
“The Shield Hero is interesting, isn’t it?”
“It doesn’t really count when you say that here. Actually, you… aren’t you acting a little weird?”

Could she be getting corrupted by the Curse Series too? After all, Taniko is active as a wielder of the Whip’s Vassal Weapons. So if she’s using weapons that are cursed to corrode the mind, her personality could easily become warped.
“Really? Maybe I made a mistake with my facial expression because I was talking to monsters with that old lady?”
“Cure… Cure.”
Little Gaelion also chirped at Taniko, and she looked down as if shocked.
“What’s wrong?”
“Gaelion said the same thing to me… I’ll try practicing a bit.”

Maybe her senses have gotten out of whack from all that fieldwork…? I’m worried about Rat, too. I’m sure we’ll be startled by his weird behavior as soon as he arrives in the village. If he suddenly starts doing the limbo or talks to us with “Uho-uhho” sounds, even I won’t be able to translate that. Even the Legendary Weapons won’t translate monster languages.
“It might be best if you take a little time off from work with Rat and learn some human manners in the village.”
“Yeah. I’ll see if I can arrange that. Even though the Sword Hero is a pain.”
Ugh… so he’s being called a pain? Poor Ren. It’s pretty doubtful this guy’s going to give me chocolate on Valentine’s Day.

By the way, Rat was in even worse shape. He’d regressed to a caveman. And to think he’s so good-looking… what a disappointing researcher. We’ve decided to have him stop fieldwork for the time being and assign him to work in the village instead. How did things get this bad in just a few months? I thought he was a level-headed guy, but maybe he really does turn into a different person when it comes to research. I’m sure Taniko got off lightly because she was returning to the village regularly.
“Well, I’ve got somewhere to go before I leave…”
“Oh? See you later, then. Alright, Gaelion, let’s study the language over here.”
“Cure…”
Although he didn’t want to, Gaelion reluctantly joined Taniko as they practiced pronunciation together.
